hero.name: Jun Tan
hero.tagline: Machine Learning Engineer | Robotics Innovator | F1 Software Developer

carousel.description: Pushing the boundaries of Reinforcement Learning and Neural Architecture Search at Imperial College London.
Developing cutting-edge on-car software systems at Mercedes-AMG HPP for the 2026 F1 Power Unit.
From autonomous rovers to invisible keyboards — building systems that bridge hardware and intelligence.

about.text: I'm Jun Tan, a Machine Learning researcher and Mechatronics engineer currently pursuing my MSc in Applied Machine Learning at Imperial College London. My journey spans from developing on-car software for Mercedes-AMG's F1 team to inventing reinforcement learning systems for stroke rehabilitation. I thrive at the intersection of intelligent algorithms and real-world engineering — whether that's optimising lap times for Formula 1, building glove-based invisible keyboards, or deploying neural networks on edge devices. I speak English, Mandarin, and Malay, and when I'm not training models, you'll find me speedcubing competitively or playing piano.

education.title: MSc Applied Machine Learning
education.description: I'm currently researching Task-based Transfer RL with a novel F-N-B factorisation approach, building algorithms that achieve few-shot and zero-shot performance on new tasks. My coursework spans LoRA fine-tuning of BERT, federated learning, neural architecture search, CUDA kernel programming, and distributed optimisation.

education.title: BEng Mechatronics Engineering
education.description: I graduated with First Class Honours (80.9%), earning the Zepler Prize in 2022 and the G-Research Prize in 2024 for being top of my class. For my dissertation, I invented Q-LEAC, a reinforcement learning stroke rehabilitation system that cut live training time by over 50% compared to traditional methods, and was tested on real patients.

work.title: Software & Controls Engineer
work.description: I spearheaded the development and maintenance of on-car software systems for the 2026 F1 Power Unit, ensuring optimal thread balancing and processor loadings across all ECU cores. I worked closely with the Lap Simulation team on energy deployment optimisers to extract lap time gains, and implemented low-level Simulink code for engine operations, chassis, and brake control with SiL/HiL verification.

work.title: Energy Storage & Engineering Intern
work.description: I delivered a full-stack HMI dashboard for energy harvest/deployment visualisation with a backend API server connecting to a localised MongoDB. I also maintained and analysed an ML prediction model for optimising efficiency of MAX300 BESS units (built from Tesla EV batteries), reducing grid energy harvesting costs by up to 24%.

work.title: Mechatronics Engineering Intern
work.description: I developed modular LabVIEW code for an automated brushbar test rig that reduced computational cost by 40%, and designed 3D-printed adapters for product compatibility across the business. I established source control practices with Bitbucket and contributed clean OOP-style code through cross-team PRs, using Confluence and Jira for agile traceability.

projects.title: Glove-based Invisible Keyboard (GIK)
projects.short_description: A pair of smart gloves that enable keyboard-free typing on any surface using deep learning.
projects.detail_description: I built a pair of gloves controlled by NanoRev2, IMUs, and FSRs to capture finger and hand movements, enabling keyboard-free typing on any surface. The custom REFFCO deep ML architecture uses attention LSTM, language model fusion, and Optuna hyperparameter tuning to process 118-dimensional sensor data and predict characters upon surface contact during live inference.

projects.title: Mase EDGE — Android DNN Optimisation
projects.short_description: A hardware-in-the-loop pipeline that optimises deep neural networks for efficient execution on Android devices.
projects.detail_description: I built a hardware-in-the-loop optimisation pipeline that automates the adaptation of deep neural network models for efficient execution on Android devices. The pipeline uses Optuna to search for optimal hyperparameters including CPU-GPU-NPU delegation ratios, followed by quantisation (QAT/PTQ) and pruning. It achieves hardware-aware deployment tailored to the user's specific Android device based on real-time model feedback.

projects.title: Autonomous Rover with SLAM
projects.short_description: A self-navigating rover with path-planning ability that achieved the highest mark ever recorded for the module.
projects.detail_description: I designed and built a self-navigating rover with SLAM-based path-planning capability using LIDAR and gyro sensors for real-time environmental feedback and control. This project achieved the highest mark ever recorded for the module at the University of Southampton.

projects.title: Q-LEAC Stroke Rehabilitation System
projects.short_description: A reinforcement learning control system for stroke rehabilitation that outperforms traditional methods.
projects.detail_description: For my BEng dissertation, I invented Q-LEAC — a MATLAB-C++ reinforcement learning control system for stroke rehabilitation. It uses Q-Learning for forearm muscle stimulation with UltraLeap camera vision feedback in a real-time deployment system, surpassing traditional model-based control methods' live training time by more than 50%. The system was tested on real patients in the hospital.

projects.title: Portfolio Website
projects.short_description: This interactive, data-driven personal portfolio website you're viewing right now.
projects.detail_description: I built this portfolio website using vanilla JavaScript, fetching all content dynamically from a JSON file. It features a git-graph visual timeline for my experience, CSS animations, a responsive grid layout, and a particle background effect — all without any frameworks.
